title: The Rivergate of the Sepik Basin
premise: August Dunmore, a salvage diver scraping a living from the Sepik River's drowned wrecks, recovers a sealed chest bearing the crest of the short-lived Republic of New Guinea — a nation that died in 1975 before anyone recognized it. Inside are documents proving a wartime gold concession was never extinguished, and every faction on the river — a fading mining consortium, a government minister, and the descendants of the men who hid it — wants August to be their instrument. Forced to guide an expedition upriver under a ticking permit deadline, he assembles a crew of outcasts who become the family he never had, while concealing what the chest truly contains. At the drowned mission of Vunapope, August must choose between claiming the fortune that would erase his debts and burning the concession forever; he burns it, tells the truth at last, and brings his people home alive, poorer and finally free.
about_author: Oscar Sandoval is the pen name of a former merchant marine officer who spent six years running supply runs along Papua New Guinea's river systems before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about men and women whose survival depends on knowing exactly when to lie.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: August's POV. Diving a navy-sealed wreck in the Sepik's lower reaches, August salvages scrap for a broker who pays in silence. A near-drowning establishes the river's indifference and August's competence, loneliness, and debt to the broker, Kessler. Emotional beat: weary endurance — a man surviving, not living.

chapters.title: Crest of a Dead Nation
chapters.summary: August's POV. His dredge snags a lead-lined chest stamped with the Republic of New Guinea seal. He opens it alone: maps, a concession deed, and letters naming a hidden cache. Fear arrives not at the treasure but at how many people will kill for paper. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Kessler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: August's POV. Kessler offers to buy the chest's contents cheap, and August realizes Kessler already knows what it is. A veiled threat makes clear refusal has costs. August hides the deed in a tarpon-slimed fuel drum. Beat: the trap closing — survival now means deception.

chapters.title: The Minister's Invitation
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilana Verrec, a land-claims lawyer representing the Karawari descendants, intercepts a government memo about the chest. Minister Okuk summons her, offering legitimacy if she finds the 'heirs' before the consortium does. Beat: cold ambition — Ilana sees the river as leverage, not home.

chapters.title: Concession Permits Expire in Forty Days
chapters.summary: August's POV. Consortium surveyor Bram Houtman arrives with permits that lapse in forty days and a contract: guide an expedition to the coordinates in the deed or lose everything to Kessler's creditors. August signs, telling himself he'll control the route. Beat: reluctant complicity.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: August's POV. He recruits a boat pilot, Meja, a disgraced nurse; Tobe, a teenage engine thief; and old Enoch, a Karawari elder who recognizes the deed's signatory as his grandfather. The found family begins forming around shared distrust of the paymasters. Beat: cautious warmth.

chapters.title: Ilana Boards at Angoram
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ilana joins the expedition claiming ministerial oversight; she and August circle each other, each hiding knowledge of the chest. Enoch watches her with unreadable patience. First night anchor, crocodiles eyes on black water. Beat: tension of mutual concealment.

chapters.title: The Middle Sepik Turns Against Us
chapters.summary: Meja's POV. Rising water, a snapped winch, and a village that refuses them passage test the crew. Tobe nearly drowns; August goes back in after him against Houtman's protest. The crew stops being employees. Beat: first bond forged in danger.

chapters.title: What Enoch Remembers
chapters.summary: Enoch's POV. Around a fire, Enoch tells the story of 1974: soldiers, a German missionary's barge, and men who sank the gold rather than surrender it to a republic that never lived. He knows where the coordinates lead — and that his grandfather helped sink it. Beat: grief and inheritance.

chapters.title: Kessler's Second Boat
chapters.summary: August's POV. A gunmetal launch shadows them through the sawgrass. August realizes Kessler sold the route to Okuk's rivals. Radio sabotage forces a detour into uncharted channels. Beat: paranoia — the wilderness is no longer the only predator.

chapters.title: Houtman's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilana's POV. Ilana discovers Houtman's real orders: recover the gold, then ensure no witnesses hold claims — including hers. She weighs warning August against protecting her own position. She copies the ledger instead. Beat: moral compromise deepening.

chapters.title: The Drowned Mission
chapters.summary: August's POV. They reach Vunapope, a mission church swallowed by a channel shift, its bell tower breaking the current. The deed's coordinates point beneath the altar. First dive reveals a flooded crypt and bones arranged deliberately — a message, not a grave. Beat: awe and violation.

chapters.title: Forty Days Become Nine
chapters.summary: Meja's POV. Flood season closes in; the return route will vanish. Houtman demands they raise the cache immediately despite the risk. August stalls by falsifying sonar readings, buying time but spending trust when Tobe catches him lying. Beat: the cost of secrets inside the family.

chapters.title: Okuk Comes Upriver
chapters.summary: Ilana's POV. The minister arrives by helicopter with armed escorts, revealing he and Kessler were partners all along. He offers August citizenship, money, erasure of his past — for the deed and silence. August understands he was always disposable. Beat: betrayal crystallized.

chapters.title: Night Assault at the Crypt
chapters.summary: August's POV. Kessler's launch and Okuk's escorts converge. In a chaotic night fight among the submerged pews, Enoch is shot covering Tobe's escape, and the crypt entrance is blasted open. The gold is visible — stacked, rusted, real. Beat: terror and sacrifice.

chapters.title: Enoch's Choice
chapters.summary: Enoch's POV. Dying, Enoch gives August his grandfather's final letter: the gold was cursed only because men let it be. He asks August to end the claim so no more Karawari die for it. Beat: passing of the burden — found family made kin by loss.

chapters.title: The Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: August's POV. Alone in the crypt with the hoist rigged, August holds a bar in each hand and calculates the life it would buy. Then he hears Houtman's men returning early — to bury witnesses. He floods the crypt charges meant for salvage. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Burning the Concession
chapters.summary: Ilana's POV. Ilana broadcasts the ledger and the deed's fraud over the expedition radio to every station on the band, destroying the permit's legal basis. Okuk's escort mutinies rather than die for a dead claim. Houtman flees into the flood. Beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: Running the Flood
chapters.summary: Meja's POV. The descent: nine days of floodwater, a crippled engine, and Kessler's launch making one last run at them in the narrows. Tobe's jury-rigged repair saves them; the launch founders on a sandbar that wasn't there yesterday. Beat: the river forgives nothing — but spares those who respect it.

chapters.title: Testimony at Angoram
chapters.summary: August's POV. August gives a full statement — the chest, the lies, the deaths — accepting prosecution rather than another silence. Ilana files the Karawari claim on the mission lands, not the gold. Kessler is arrested ashore. Beat: reckoning; identity reclaimed through honesty.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tobe's POV. Weeks later, the crew salvages ordinary wrecks again. Tobe, apprenticed to Meja, dives the Vunapope channel and finds only the bell, which they raise for Enoch's village. Some things should stay down; some should come home. Beat: quiet healing.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the mouth where the Sepik meets the sea, August scatters Enoch's letter and takes a new charter — Ilana, Meja, and Tobe aboard, no secrets left between them. He is still poor, still marked, but no longer alone. Final beat: found family as the only treasure worth keeping.
